pages.transcription:
18.5.1941 (Hotel Wyndham 42 West 58 Street)
Dear Hannah & Manfred, I have just your kind cable. You have
nothing missed, all these lectures are without importance and
~~are~~ altogether we minutes instead of tea. Lotte was sitting
on the grand table between Somerset Maugham and Conte Sforza
I suppose she has proved a brilliant conversationalist. Today I
have time to write {you} as she has gone to Croton and you will get
from her farther news about your pet. I believe that the asthma
treatment will soon ~~better~~ bring her complete relief for a long
time or for ever; she is already quite well, makes long walks
sleeps without to wake up a single time. And that she likes
to stay a little longer in the morning hours has nothing to do
with her asthma but it a kind of 'Blitzgift' she brought into her
marriage. I do nothing to drive her out only I refuse to make
the morning coffee myself. Now we are wondering where to go
during the months of heat. It is not at all easy because we
who have no car are something prehistoric in this country -
all is adapted for driving. Then ~~all~~ is so far away and Lotte
has probably to ~~go~~ form and to look if she finds something con-
venient. I personally has liked to stay here provided we had found
a hotel with air conditioning, but the very few, which have such.
roofs are too expensive and too fashionable for my taste. Even
if I would calculate that four hours saves for work every day would
match the expenses I could not feel alright in such a kind
of Claridges - I never did even in the times when it was
possible. Again and again, we can make ~~not~~ ~~disturb~~ 
plans and who can do so in this moment - since years
we believe always that next month next year one shall see
clear but it seems that we shall pass the greater and
certainly the best part of our life with waiting, fearing, hoping
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf dünnem Papier. Violette Tinte. Die Zeilenumbrüche folgen dem Original.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Keine eigene Transkription.

pages.transcription:
Lotte had a very nice letter from Miss Bales, she has the intention
to go over for her long holidays but Lord Halifax himself advised
her not to do so - it is practically impossible to travel nowadays
within time-limits and it is not advisable. We were so sorry
to hear from her that also our dear Bath had on holy Friday a
hint of air-raid; but I am convinced it is a better place than
London and we are anxious to know you there. Manfred will
want his rest after the examinations and yourself Hannah, you
must be somewhat worn out. In Bath you can at least rest the
whole day long in the garden, while London like every big town
also does not allow to relax; you will have telefone and
guests and whatever. - Now to Friedental. I am in touch
with his friend Margaret Raiser who is very active to get him
an affidavit and I do the best for my part. Here it would be
easy to get for him something to do. The most important
is now to have the affidavit ready and to try for a passage
- also for Heinrich Mayer we have made inquiries about the
validity of his affidavit. To Friedental we did send a
food parcel, let us hope that he will get it, meanwhile I expect
you will have got yours already. It is a pity that one has
to take those ready-mades and cannot choose, but it seems
that there is an arrangement to use only one type of
food-parcel to avoid all specifications of weight and cus-
toms and so she did try this out. Now dear Hannah I
know all this is not very interesting for you because you
are waiting already to hear from me and this you shall
through Lotte immediately she comes back from Croton
I understand how heartbreaking it must be to you not to
be near to her. There is a possibility to let British children
speak by wireless to her daddies and mammies but I suppose you

pages.notes: Scan mit Farbskala und Grauskala. Text identisch mit Seite 3 (ohne die Randnotizen, da diese durch die Skalen verdeckt oder nicht erfasst sind). Die Transkription konzentriert sich auf den Haupttext.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur und der violetten Tinte. Die Randnotizen auf Seite 3 wurden korrekt zugeordnet.
